moduleRecord.stated: not warranted on this verdict; the title, terms and e >= 0.05 questions are listed for the coordinator in case the finding is reconsidered
moduleRecord.title: propagator/sdn-ap: J3-J5 first-order short-period terms (m = 0, j >= 2, small-e form in the argument of latitude) and the J3/J5 constant normal member at the output step; the J2 second-order short-period terms (Kozai 1962) as a second, derived item
moduleRecord.terms: J2-J5-SHORT-PERIOD.md items 2a, 2b and 3: per object a table of 12 floats (the forced Hill response per harmonic j = 2..5 of the J3-J5 force harmonics at the mean a, i, n) plus the constant normal member N0 (1 float), rebuilt when the mean i or a moves, applied to the osculating output position in RTN; the j = 1 members stay in the rates as today; the J2 second-order short-period terms transcribed from Kozai 1962 with their own reference-side validation (this record bounds them, P2)
eGte005Questions: the q = +-1 sidebands (Kaula G_lpq) of the J3-J5 members at e >= 0.05: (l + 2) e / 2 reaches 0.175 at e 0.05 and 0.35 at e 0.1 for l = 5, and the e grid rows here state the measured degradation

the identity of the J3 and J5 j = 1 members with the module's odd-degree long-period rates (w = +-1) at e >= 0.05, where the once-per-revolution term is no longer the small-eccentricity-vector response
the constant normal member at e >= 0.05: whether it stays a constant in position or becomes the j = 1 (i, Omega) short-period term of the elements
the wide-e class above kWideE 0.3: whether the J3-J5 zonal members enter the existing (l, 0, p, q) grid or stay in this table

the radial bias at fixed mean motion R0 in the polar regimes (Sentinel-3, CryoSat-2), which the J4 constant member does not explain and the Z2 arm locates: the J2 second-order mean-to-osculating radius or the mean-element convention
